message.content: I have full source and problem context already. I'll record the description model for this log1p kernel.

function.arguments: {"contract_model": ["Target[i] = log(1 + x[i]) on the exact stored FP16 value, computed in real arithmetic; output is fresh FP32 tensor [N] on x.device.", "Absolute tolerance 1e-6 per element, zero relative tolerance, signed zeros equivalent; single verdict over the entire legal domain, not per-distribution.", "Domain: 1D contiguous FP16 [N], 1<=N<=131072, CUDA, ordinary tensor flags; every finite FP16 value strictly > -1 is legal, including signed zeros, subnormals, the smallest value above -1 (-0.99951171875... actually nextabove -1 in FP16 is -0.99951), and 65504.", "validate_inputs() must enforce the domain and run() must call it; reference() uses FP64 library log1p; make_inputs() examples only.", "Frozen environment: NVIDIA T4, PyTorch 2.8.0, Triton 3.4.0."], "kernel_model": ["Loads FP16 x, casts to FP32, computes u=1+x and an FP32 correction term div_rn(x-(u-1),u) to compensate rounding in u (log1p-style Cody-Waite compensation).", "Bitcasts u to uint32 to extract exponent and mantissa, normalizes mantissa to [1,2) then halves it when >1.65 so the atanh-series argument z=(m-1)/(m+1) stays small; z in roughly [0, ~0.245].", "Computes log(u) = exponent*ln2 (split into high/low parts 0.69313812256 and 0.0000090580006145) + 2z*P(z^2), a short odd rational polynomial (coeffs 1/3, 1/5, 1/7 truncated to 0.33333, 0.2, 0.142857).", "Final value = high + (local_log + (low + correction)); stores FP32 with mask; BLOCK=256, num_warps=4, enable_fp_fusion=False (to control rounding), N as constexpr.", "validate_inputs mirrors the stated domain: finite, x > -1, FP16, 1D contiguous, size bounds, ordinary flags; run() calls it and allocates output on x.device."], "risk_map": ["Polynomial accuracy: the series 2z*(1+z^2*(1/3+z^2*(1/5+z^2*(1/7)))) truncated at 1/7 with rounded coefficients (0.33333, 0.2, 0.142857 not 0.142857142857) may exceed 1e-6 absolute error, since |z| can reach ~0.245 after the 1.65 halving rule; truncation error of order z^9/9 is tiny but coefficient rounding of 0.142857 (~1.4e-6 relative) times z^2 ~ 0.06 contributes ~4e-8... but 0.33333 vs 1/3 error ~3.3e-6 absolute times 2z ~ 0.49 gives ~1.6e-7 — needs numeric check; boundary near u=1.65 where z jumps between reduction regimes.", "log2(ln2) split: high=0.69313812256, low=0.0000090580006145 sums to 0.69314718056... vs true ln2=0.693147180559945; residual ~1e-10*exponent, fine up to exponent ~15 (x up to 65504 gives u up to 65505, exponent ~15) — small.", "Cancellation for x near -1: u = 1+x is exact in FP32 for FP16 x near -1 (Sterbenz), so u can be as small as the next FP16 above -0.0? Actually x>-1 means u>0; smallest u ~ 4.88e-4 (FP16 -0.9995 -> u ~ 4.8828e-4) — exponent ~-11; z from mantissa in [1,2) fine. But if u subnormal in FP32? No, u>=~4.8e-4 is normal. However for x values like -0.9995, correction = (x - (u-1))/u: u-1 is computed in FP32 and is inexact for u near 1 only; near u=4.8e-4 rounding pattern differs — needs probe.", "Coefficient 0.2 is not a rounded power (1/5=0.2 exact in decimal but 0.2 is not exact in binary); tiny.", "The mantissa normalization uses |u| bits: u>0 always here, but for u in (0.5,1) exponent extraction handles it; for u subnormal in FP32 (impossible here since x FP16 >-1 gives u >= ~2^-11) fine. Edge: u exactly 1.0 (x=0): exponent 0, mantissa 1.0, z=0, correction 0 — output 0, correct for signed zeros.", "Rounding of x - (u - 1.0): for |x| < 2^-11 subnormal FP16, 1+x rounds and correction compensates; check correction formula's own rounding for subnormal x (e.g. x=5.96e-8, log1p ~ 5.96e-8; correction = (x-(u-1))/u where u-1 may be 0 or 2^-24 steps — possible loss below tolerance? absolute tolerance 1e-6 makes tiny x trivially pass).", "Potential Triton fp32 constant folding/fusion issues mitigated by enable_fp_fusion=False; verify it applies.", "Threshold 1.65 mantissa split changes which path z takes; verify continuity/accuracy on both sides."], "open_questions": ["Does the truncated polynomial with rounded coefficients (esp. 0.33333, 0.2, 0.142857) keep worst-case absolute error <= 1e-6 across the full u range? Needs runtime sweep, e.g. exhaustive FP16 > -1 (~32K values) compared to FP64 log1p.", "Is accuracy preserved at the mantissa=1.65 split boundary and for u near the extremes (smallest u from x next above -1; u=65505)"], "scope_notes": ["The 1e-6 is ABSOLUTE tolerance; since |log1p| grows to ~11.1 at x=65504, absolute tolerance is generous at large x and tight near x=0 (target ~x for tiny x, error must stay < 1e-6 — easy since values are tiny).", "Exhaustive verification over all legal FP16 values > -1 is feasible (~32k values), giving a complete-domain correctness experiment.", "Correctness is one global verdict; a single failing element suffices to reject; passing benign random inputs is weak evidence."], "summary": "Describer model for case_166: FP16 log1p Triton kernel using exponent range reduction plus a truncated atanh-series polynomial, targeting 1e-6 absolute tolerance over all finite FP16 inputs > -1."}
